headerDisplay: Exposes an Eight Sleep Pod running the free-sleep firmware to Apple HomeKit. `host` is the only field most installs need. `sides`, the poll/write timing overrides, the No Response delay, keep-alive, the water-low sensor type, and the four hub-service toggles (prime, LED, test alarm, server fault) are live; the remaining fields are reserved for a future release and have no effect yet.

host.title: Pod Host
host.description: The Pod's LAN hostname or IP address, e.g. 192.168.1.50.

deviceWriteDebounceMs.title: Device-lane write debounce (ms) — governs the Pod LED's brightness-drag coalescing specifically; other writes use the write debounce above

waterLowSensorType.title: Water-low sensor type — the hub always publishes a water-low sensor; this chooses which HomeKit service type represents it

keepAlive.title: Keep-alive
keepAlive.description: Periodically re-arms a side's 12-hour on-duration while it is on, so 'on' never silently expires overnight.

keepAliveMs.title: Keep-alive re-arm duration (ms)
keepAliveMs.description: Must be strictly greater than the re-arm threshold below. This UI cannot enforce that relationship between two separate fields — an invalid combination is caught by the plugin at Homebridge startup, which fails to load rather than silently accepting it.

keepAliveThresholdMs.title: Keep-alive re-arm threshold (ms)
keepAliveThresholdMs.description: A side is re-armed once its remaining time drops below this. Must be strictly less than the re-arm duration above — this UI cannot enforce that cross-field relationship, so an invalid combination is instead caught loudly at Homebridge startup. Minimum 120000ms (2 min): below that, the plugin's internally-derived check cadence can no longer catch every side before it expires (see src/config.ts).

awayModeWritePolicy.title: Away-mode write policy — governs a write to either side while one side has away mode on: mirror the change with a second real POST /api/deviceStatus to the other side (updating its cached state to match), or block the write

primeSwitch.title: Pod Prime switch
primeSwitch.description: Publishes a hub switch that starts a prime cycle when turned on. The Pod has no stop command, so turning it off is refused rather than sent. Off by default — priming is loud and runs for minutes.

ledLightbulb.title: Pod LED lightbulb
ledLightbulb.description: Publishes a hub lightbulb controlling the Pod's LED brightness. Every write re-posts the Pod's full device-settings object, debounced by the device-lane write debounce below (minimum 500ms) — a brightness drag can take up to roughly the fast-poll window (default ~5s) to visibly settle in the Home app, since this field has no optimistic feedback. Off by default.

testAlarmSwitch.title: Pod Test Alarm switches
testAlarmSwitch.description: Publishes two momentary hub switches, Test Alarm Left and Test Alarm Right, that each manually trigger the Pod's alarm vibration for that side only, overriding away mode and power state. Each tile self-resets to off after about a second regardless of outcome; the physical vibration itself lasts at least 10 seconds. Off by default.

serverFaultSensor.title: Pod Server Fault sensor
serverFaultSensor.description: Publishes a hub sensor reflecting the Pod's own self-reported subsystem health. Polled on the slow cadence, only while enabled — the endpoint is not free. Off by default.
